He declared for the NBA Draft April 13th, 2015, forgoing his senior year. ==College career== Anderson originally verbally committed to [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] but later changed his commitment following [[Gary Williams|Gary Williams']] retirement.{{cite web|title=Patience, practice propelled Justin Anderson to starring role at Virginia|url=http://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/01/14/justin-anderson-virginia-cavaliers-acc|accessdate=2015-03-30|date=2015-01-14|publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} On May 26, 2011, Anderson signed his [[National Letter of Intent]] to play for [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]]. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2012}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Justin Anderson | position = [[Small Forward|SF]] | hometown = Montross, Virginia | highschool = [[Montrose Christian School]] | feet = 6 | inches = 6 | weight = 207 | 40 = | commitdate = 2011-5-26 | rivals stars = 4 | scout stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2012 | rivals ref title = Virginia 2012 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = 2012 Virginia Commits | espn ref title = ESPN | 247 ref title = Virginia 2012 Basketball Commits | rivals school = virginia-8 | scout s = 75 | espn schoolid = 258 | 247 school = http://virginia.247sports.com/Season/2012-Basketball/Commits | scout overall = 63 | rivals overall = 35 | espn overall = 49 | 247 overall = 51 | accessdate = 2015-03-30 | bball = yes }} Anderson primarily played off the bench his first two seasons at Virginia. His play during his sophomore year garnered him an ACC Sixth Man of the Year Award. Following the graduation of [[Joe Harris (basketball)|Joe Harris]], Anderson was inserted into the starting lineup. A fractured finger against [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]] and an appendectomy forced Anderson to miss the last 8 games of the regular season but he returned in time for Virginia's first game in the [[2015 ACC Men's Basketball Tournament|ACC Tournament]]. After putting up career high numbers in scoring and other offensive categories, Anderson was named second-team All-ACC and third-team All-American by the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]]. On April 13, 2015 Anderson declared for the 2015 [[NBA]] draft, forgoing his senior year.
